contexts.text: The breads of proposition (or show-bread).
Are they not averse to the mere proposition?
From consent, then from purpose...
When anyone proposes anything to himself, he perceives it as present...
The twelve breads of proposition = the good of celestial love; and their being cooked in cakes = the goods of spiritual love.
Proposition with influx. Signified.
Those injure anyone not from purpose... Signified, Explained.
When a man shall act from purpose against his companion () = previous thought from a depraved will. Explained.
Not purposed and deliberate... CL 395.
Their evils have been... not from purpose against the truth...
This combat is not grievous except with those who... have indulged in their concupiscences from purpose.
Take the falsest thing, and put it into a proposition...
Those things of the mind which belong to any purposed Thing are in the middle...
If he thinks that this evil is contrary to the commandments... he then commits it from purpose, and thereby lets himself deeply down, from which he cannot be brought out except by actual repentance.
In the order set forth.
They confirmed the Truth of the proposition...
The end, purpose, or intention of the will is primarily regarded by the Lord; and therefore so far as a man is in these... he is initiated into purity.
With these a conjugial life is their purpose, intention, or end... (and therefore) is such before the Lord.
The Angels replied that they regard all from the purpose, intention, or end... CL 527:end. TCR 523:end.
(These adulteries) are imputed to them as evils of purpose... Explained.

That which flows forth from the very essence of a man's life, thus that which flows forth from his will or love, is principally called purpose; but that which flows forth from... his understanding, is called intention.
That adulteries from the purpose of the will... render men natural, sensuous, and corporeal. Explained.
All things done by a man's interior will, are done from purpose; because that will proposes to itself what it does by its intention.
He who from purpose or confirmation acts against one commandment acts against the rest. Explained. TCR 523.
If from purpose and confirmation they abstain from one evil because it is a sin, they abstain from all evils. Explained.
A man comes into this purpose, if once or twice in a year he examines himself, and repents of the evil he discovers.
Purposed evils (are included in the eighth commandment). TCR 322. TCR 324.
This proposition and discussion are rarely terminated in the affirmative...
This infinite diversity... derives its origin from the end, intention, and consequent purpose...
In the seed are concealed the end, intention, and purpose of producing fruits...

Into this purpose (to act against the commandments) come those who do not want to hear anything about repentance; but into the purpose of believing in the Lord and of loving the neighbour, come those who through repentance have removed some evils which are sins: these are kept by the Lord in the purpose to abstain from other evils; and therefore if they commit sin from ignorance or overpowering concupiscence, it is not imputed to them...
With full purpose of amendment of life.
If you do so from any other purpose or end...
The truth of the proposition is evident...
As the end is the purpose, and this intends, purpose is also of the will, and it enters the understanding by the intention...
Some assume certain propositions... but others see that they are hypotheses.
A dispute about this proposition...
Things which suit their theses or propositions.
That we should not propose to ourselves to do anything for certain which is in itself indifferent...
When this proposition had been confirmed by the Angels.
They can induce others to believe whatever they propose to themselves.
It was then proposed to (them) to solve this proposition...
They set forth with a mere regard to wealth.
They never desist from a purpose once formed. SE 4745.
Those who have been homicides from will and purpose...
Those who act against them from purpose. Signified.
The first proposition is believed without being first explored... AE 824:2.
By deceit = from purpose. AE 866:6. AE 866:8.
